To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IFN-gamma up-regulated IR2 in human esophageals, and then IR2 decreased IFNGR1 expression to promote cell growth and inhibit apoptosis.
IFN-gamma inhibits cell growth in esophageal cells by upregulating IRF-2 and downregulating IFNGR1.

IFN-gamma induces IRF-2, which suppresses IFNGR1 and then inhibits IFN-gamma signaling, and that the negative regulation of IRF-1 by IRF-2 may be a mechanism for IFN-alpha/beta resistance in esophageal carcinoma.

the regulatory mechanism of IFN-gamm...
the molecular mechanisms of IFN-gammadependent pathways in esophageal tumors, which may provide a novel insight for esophageal cancer treatment.
the roles of IFN-gammadependent pathway in esophagecal cancer cells and the potential mechanisms of IFN-gammaregulation in human esophagecal cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IRF-1 and IFNGR2 are tumor suppressors, whereas IRF-2 is a tumor promoter in esophageal carcinogenesis.

IRF-1, IRF-3, and IRF-7, as the positive regulators for IFN-gammadependent pathway, were up-regulated in esophageal carcinogenesis, while IRF-2, as the negative regulator for IFN-gammadependent pathway, was up-regulated in advanced esophageal cancers, and the balance between positive and negative regulators for IFN- gamma pathway was disrupted in esophageal tumors.
IRF-1 and IRF-7 are positive mediators for IFN-g pathway, whereas IRF-2 is a negative mediator for the same pathway in human esophagealcancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IRF-1/2-mediated negative feedback regulation of IFNGR/STAT1 signaling is an important pathway for the functions of interferons in esophageal carcinogenesis.

IRF-1 and IRF-3, which were up-regulated by IFN-gamma, might activate the expression of IFNGR, whereas IRF-2, which was also up-regulated by the IFN-gammadependent pathway, might repress the transcription of IFNGR and thus inhibit the sensitivity of cancer cells to IFNGR.
IFN-gamma/IRF-2/IFNGR1 axis may be a potential therapeutic target for esophageal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRF-2 level is an important indicator for the prognosis of patients with esophageal cancer, and IRF-1/IRF-2 ratio may be an indicator for the efficacy of IFN-g therapy in esophageal carcinoma.
the IFNGR1/IRF-2/IFN-gamma pathway is a negative feedback regulation system in esophageal carcinomas, which may provide a new insight into the development of esophageal cancers.
the negative feedback regulation of IFNGR by IRF-2 in esophagea cancer cells might be an important mechanism for tumor progression.
